prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation; automation covers bay monitoring/control, station coordination, external interfaces; protection/primary equipment stay under approved designs. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): bay sequencing, permissives/interlocks; produces Bay Status Digest; timestamps local state changes; requests breaker operations from Breaker Control Unit only if mode/permissives allow. North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller automate station portions. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem): independent local protection, approved setting group; produces Relay Diagnostic Note (used by Larkspur in fault analysis). Breaker Control Unit: executes authorized operations, authoritative local interlocks. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing): operator interface; current indications kept separate from archive evidence; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; no protection. Station Gateway bounds external/remote comms. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin): time alignment; produces Clock Drift Snapshot; reference loss means holdover, affects interpretation, evidence not discarded. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard): authoritative evidence as received (source, event/receipt time, quality); keeps order; flags uncertain time/sequence; corrected/estimated times distinguishable; keeps admin/access history; role-limited, auditable; retention per schedule; investigation holds block deletion; health/restore checks; protected backup copy. Engineering Workstation: revision-controlled config, engineering-only; search/filter/export tools; produces Settings Review Receipt. Maintenance Remote Terminal: approved maintenance only. Station DC System: control power (loss hits visibility/timing); produces Battery Load Test Record. Actors: Control Room Operator: directs, suspends work, authorizes return to automation, reviews archived sequences, submits switching requests (equipment, state changes, timing) to Keystone. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone): station-wide switching plan across both bays; checks requests vs clearances/work; confirms clearance and handback. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): settings vs study, independent second reviewer; compares event times/relay indications. Substation Field Crew (Cinder): authorized work, verifies identity; sends Breaker Inspection Tag. Substation Supervisor confirms procedures. Requirements: local control precedence; remote commands permission/interlock checked; unique revision IDs; no copied-value approval; pre-deploy model/firmware check; work windows; post-install checks; discrepancies halt release; stale data confirmed; field/control-room mismatch unsafe; stop on comms loss; bounded queries; exports keep timestamps/flags, interpretations and conclusions separate from evidence.

New part:
S127: The Substation Supervisor resolves priority conflicts and confirms the operational authority for exceptional switching conditions.
S128: Approved switching sequences identify the required order of actions, hold points, and conditions for stopping work.
S129: The North Bay Controller manages control and interlocking functions assigned to the north bay under the approved sequence.
S130: The North Bay Controller blocks a close command when its local interlocks indicate that the bay is not ready.
S131: The South Bay Controller manages the corresponding control and interlocking functions assigned to the south bay.
S132: The two controllers have separate equipment scopes and do not substitute for one another when executing a switching sequence.
S133: The bay boundary defines which controller may operate each device and which indications are used to confirm its state.
S134: Equipment shared across the boundary requires explicit coordination before a switching action can affect either bay.
S135: The Bay Automation Controller presents bay control status while preserving the separate operating scopes of the two controllers.
S136: The Breaker Control Unit executes permitted breaker commands only when the applicable control conditions are satisfied.
S137: The North Protection Panel supports protection functions for the north-side equipment within its assigned scope.
S138: The Transformer Protection Panel retains its protection authority independently of the bay switching sequence.
S139: The Station Supervisory Control System uses the status digest to review current station operating conditions.
S140: The Sequence Event Archive receives the Clock Drift Snapshot for event-time correlation.
S141: The Switching Desk Coordinator produces the Isolation Boundary Card for the planned work.
S142: The Station Gateway produces the Protocol Retry Summary for communication review.
S143: Larkspur reviews protection coordination questions that could affect the planned switching sequence.
S144: Bluefin provides the station time reference used to align recorded event times.
S145: The Substation Field Crew confirms device identity and local conditions before carrying out an authorized operation.
S146: After the Switching Desk Coordinator confirms operational handback, state-change evidence remains available for authorized engineering review.
S147: Alarm indications are assessed according to protection significance, equipment condition, and the potential effect on service.
S148: The Control Room Operator reviews the alarm priority, source, time, and associated bay indications before deciding on a response.
S149: The operator distinguishes a new alarm from a standing condition and checks whether related indications support the same assessment.
S150: For a protection operation or an unexplained equipment state, the Control Room Operator treats the condition as requiring prompt investigation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
